docs.d: Flutter versions for every project.

s.b: FVM lets each project use its own Flutter version. Install an SDK once and share it across projects that use the same version.

1. Install FVM on your computer. 2. Set up your project and choose its Flutter version. 3. Run fvm flutter and fvm dart from the project directory. You do not need Dart or Flutter installed before installing FVM.
fvm flutter pub get fvm flutter run fvm flutter test fvm dart analyze Want to type just flutter? Follow Shell Setup.

Change a project's Flutter version. Set a default for other directories. Find available Flutter releases. Update FVM or Flutter. Run your project in CI. Fix setup or SDK selection problems. Documentation for AI assistants is also available.

docs.d: Install FVM on macOS, Linux, or Windows without an existing Dart or Flutter SDK.

s.h: Install FVM on macOS or Linux
s.b: Run the install script: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrgnhnt96/fvm/main/install.sh sh You need curl, an unzip tool (unzip or Python 3), and a checksum tool (sha256sum, shasum, or openssl). You do not need Dart or Flutter first. Run the setup command printed by the installer. With the default install location, it is: "$HOME/.fvm/bin/fvm" setup --write-path-line Close and reopen your terminal, then check the installation: fvm --version If the installer reports an existing fvm shell function or alias, follow its instructions to remove the conflict before running setup.

1. Open FVM releases and choose a release containing fvm-windows-x64.zip. 2. Download that ZIP and its matching .sha256 file. In PowerShell, run Get-FileHash .\fvm-windows-x64.zip -Algorithm SHA256 and compare the hash with the .sha256 file. 3. Extract fvm.exe to a permanent folder, such as C:\Tools\fvm. 4. Run setup using the full path: & "C:\Tools\fvm\fvm.exe" setup Add the executable's folder and the shims folder printed by setup to your user PATH in Windows Environment Variables. Put the shims folder before any other Flutter installation. Open a new terminal and run fvm --version. Windows setup prints the paths to add; --write-path-line is not available for PowerShell.

On macOS or Linux, set FVM_HOME when running the installer: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrgnhnt96/fvm/main/install.sh FVM_HOME="$HOME/tools/fvm" sh Also set FVM_HOME to that same directory in your shell startup file for future commands. Run the setup command printed by this installation. To install a specific FVM release, set FVM_VERSION to a version listed on FVM releases: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrgnhnt96/fvm/main/install.sh FVM_VERSION=" " sh Replace before running the command.
Follow Quick Start to install Flutter and select your project's version.

docs.d: Choose Flutter for your project, configure your editor, and run your app.

s.b: Install FVM first. Run the following commands from your Flutter project's root directory.

fvm install stable fvm use stable --gitignore fvm flutter --version install stable downloads the current stable Flutter release. use stable saves that release's version number in .fvmrc, so the project stays on it until you choose another version. To use a particular release instead: fvm use 3.44.0 --gitignore use downloads the version if it is missing. Find other available versions with fvm list-remote. Commit .fvmrc and the .gitignore change so teammates use the same version. The .fvm/ directory stays out of Git.

For VS Code, add this setting to your project's .vscode/settings.json (merge it with any existing settings): { "dart.flutterSdkPath": ".fvm/flutter_sdk" } For Android Studio or IntelliJ, set the Flutter SDK path to the full path of your project's .fvm/flutter_sdk directory. Restart the editor if it still shows the previous SDK.
fvm flutter pub get fvm flutter run fvm flutter test fvm dart analyze After shell setup, you can also run plain flutter from this directory.

Open its .fvmrc and run fvm use with the version shown there. For example, if it contains {"flutter": "3.44.0"}: fvm use 3.44.0 fvm flutter pub get This installs the SDK if needed and creates the editor's SDK link on your computer. Running fvm flutter alone does not install a missing SDK.
Run fvm use with the new version and commit the updated .fvmrc. To use a newer stable release, repeat both fvm install stable and fvm use stable.

docs.d: Make the flutter command use your project’s selected SDK.

s.b: Shell setup lets you type flutter instead of fvm flutter. If you already ran setup during installation and reopened your terminal, you can skip this step. On macOS or Linux with the default installation: "$HOME/.fvm/bin/fvm" setup --write-path-line Setup backs up your shell startup file and adds the required PATH entries. Open a new terminal afterward. On Windows, run fvm setup and add the printed directories to your user PATH in Environment Variables. See Installation if fvm is not yet available.

From a project where you have run fvm use: flutter --version fvm which fvm doctor FVM's launcher, called a shim, must come before other Flutter installations on PATH. If the wrong Flutter runs, follow the corrections printed by fvm doctor.

Run fvm setup to create the launcher and print the PATH instructions for your shell. Follow those instructions instead of using --write-path-line if you manage your startup file yourself. Keep the FVM executable in its installed location. If you move it, run setup again using its new path.
Use fvm dart for the Dart version included with your selected Flutter SDK: fvm dart --version Setup does not change plain dart. If you use DVM, see Using FVM alongside DVM.
fvm setup --remove-path-line Open a new terminal afterward. This removes the line added by --write-path-line; it leaves manually added PATH entries, FVM, and your SDKs in place.

docs.d: Share your project’s Flutter version with teammates.

s.b: From your project's root directory, run: fvm use 3.44.0 --gitignore FVM installs the SDK if needed and writes .fvmrc: {"flutter": "3.44.0"} Commit .fvmrc and the .gitignore change. Teammates can run fvm use 3.44.0 after cloning to install the same SDK and set up their editor link. fvm use stable and fvm use also save a concrete version number. Install a channel with fvm install stable before selecting it.

s.h: Use one version across nested directories
s.b: Commands in subdirectories use the nearest .fvmrc in that directory or a parent. Running fvm use from a subdirectory updates that same file. To give a nested project its own version, run this from the nested project's root: fvm use 3.44.0 --here --gitignore

Set your editor's Flutter SDK path to .fvm/flutter_sdk beside .fvmrc. FVM updates this link when you run fvm use. Do not commit .fvm/: each computer creates its own link. See Quick Start for editor settings.

FVM also accepts a bare version on one line, or a JSON flutter value naming a channel or alias. Those names must be available on each computer; concrete version numbers are simpler to share. If a pin is invalid or its SDK is missing, follow the error's correction or installation command. FVM will not substitute your global version.

docs.d: Choose a Flutter channel or save a short name for a version.

s.b: fvm install stable fvm use stable Install the channel first so FVM knows which release to use. fvm use stable pins that release's version number in your project. To move the project to a newer stable release, run both commands again. Installing a newer release by itself does not change the project's saved version. You can also use beta. Historical dev releases are available when listed by fvm list-remote --channel dev. FVM does not install main or master builds.

s.h: Save a name for a version
s.b: fvm alias work 3.44.0 fvm use work work is a shortcut on your computer. fvm use work saves the version number in .fvmrc, so teammates do not need your alias. List or remove your saved names: fvm alias list fvm unalias work Removing an alias leaves the SDK installed.

s.h: Use names in an existing pin
s.b: If you manually put a channel or alias in .fvmrc, FVM looks up its saved value on your computer. A channel does not fetch a newer release when you run Flutter; refresh it with fvm install stable or fvm install beta. Prefer the version number written by fvm use when sharing a project.

docs.d: Find which Flutter version will run in your current directory.

s.b: fvm which The output shows which Flutter SDK FVM selected and why. For only the executable path, use fvm which --path.

FVM uses the first selection that applies: 1. FVM_FLUTTER_VERSION, if you set this environment variable. 2. The nearest .fvmrc in your current directory or a parent directory. 3. The default you set with fvm global. 4. Another Flutter installation on your PATH. If none applies, install and select an SDK with fvm use . If an explicit selection is invalid or missing, fix that selection; FVM does not skip it to use another SDK.
fvm global 3.44.0 A project's .fvmrc still takes priority.

s.h: Override the version for one command
s.b: Install the version first. In a POSIX shell: fvm install 3.44.0 FVM_FLUTTER_VERSION=3.44.0 fvm flutter test In PowerShell: fvm install 3.44.0 $env:FVM_FLUTTER_VERSION = "3.44.0" fvm flutter test Remove-Item Env:FVM_FLUTTER_VERSION The PowerShell variable applies to the session until you remove it. Neither example changes .fvmrc. If plain flutter chooses a different SDK from fvm flutter, check Shell Setup.

docs.d: Download a Flutter SDK without changing your project’s selected version.

s.b: fvm install stable This downloads the current stable release. Select it for your project afterward with fvm use stable. To download a particular version: fvm install 3.44.0 Already installed versions are reused. Find available releases with fvm list-remote.
fvm install 3.44.0 --force Use --force (or -f) to replace an installed SDK, for example after its files are damaged.

You can pass beta or a saved alias instead of a version. Each fvm install stable or fvm install beta checks for that channel's current release. It does not change an existing project's version; run fvm use to do that.

docs.d: Choose a project’s Flutter version and configure its editor SDK link.

s.b: From the project directory: fvm use 3.44.0 --gitignore FVM installs the version if needed, writes its number to .fvmrc, and creates .fvm/flutter_sdk for your editor. --gitignore adds .fvm/ to the project's .gitignore. Commit .fvmrc and the .gitignore change. See Quick Start for editor settings.

fvm install stable fvm use stable Install the channel first. use stable saves the installed channel's version number, so later channel updates do not move this project. Saved aliases also resolve to version numbers.

s.h: Select a version for a nested project
s.b: By default, use updates the nearest existing .fvmrc in your current directory or a parent. To give the current directory its own pin: fvm use 3.44.0 --here --gitignore
fvm use --global (or -g) sets the fallback for directories without a project pin. It is equivalent to fvm global.

docs.d: Choose the Flutter version used outside pinned projects.

s.b: fvm global 3.44.0 FVM installs the version if needed. Directories with a .fvmrc keep their project version; FVM_FLUTTER_VERSION also takes priority. To use the current stable release: fvm install stable fvm global stable This saves a specific version number. Repeat both commands when you want to update the default.
fvm global To see what will run in your current directory, use fvm which.

docs.d: See which Flutter SDKs are installed on your computer.

s.b: fvm list The output identifies the current project selection and global default, along with saved aliases and channels. fvm ls is a shorter spelling of the same command.
Use fvm list-remote to see releases you can download. Use fvm remove to delete an installed version you no longer need.

docs.d: Find Flutter releases available for your computer.

s.b: fvm list-remote Shows the newest 25 stable releases available for your operating system and CPU architecture. This command requires a network connection.

s.h: Choose a channel or show all releases
s.b: fvm list-remote --channel beta fvm list-remote --all fvm list-remote --channel dev --all --channel (or -c) accepts stable, beta, or dev. --all includes older releases. Historical dev releases may be available; main and master builds are not supported.
Run fvm use to install it and select it for your project, or fvm install to download it without changing your project.

docs.d: Free disk space by deleting an installed Flutter SDK.

s.b: fvm list fvm remove 3.44.0 All projects using a version share its SDK. Check your other projects before removing it: they will need that version installed again to run.

Change the project pin, global default, or alias identified in the error, then retry. FVM can check local references but cannot find every project on your disk. To remove the SDK even when references still point to it: fvm remove 3.44.0 --force --force (or -f) leaves those references in place. Repair affected projects with fvm use or reinstall the removed version with fvm install .

docs.d: Save a short name for a Flutter version.

s.b: fvm alias work 3.44.0 fvm use work The alias is saved on your computer. fvm use work writes the version number to .fvmrc, so teammates do not need to create the same alias. Creating an alias does not install the SDK. Selecting it with fvm use installs the version if needed.
fvm alias list An alias can also name a channel or another alias. Install a channel before using it, and avoid aliases that point back to each other. Remove a name with fvm unalias.

docs.d: Delete a saved name without deleting its Flutter SDK.

s.b: fvm unalias work The SDK remains installed. Projects pinned to a concrete version keep working. If you manually put this alias in .fvmrc, replace it by running fvm use . Other aliases that refer to the removed name also need updating. To remove the SDK itself, use fvm remove.

docs.d: See which Flutter SDK will run and why it was selected.

s.b: fvm which Shows the version and whether it came from an environment override, a project pin, your global default, or PATH. fvm current runs the same command.
fvm which --path Use this when a script needs the path to the Flutter executable. If the result is unexpected, see Resolution Order or run fvm doctor.

docs.d: Run Flutter using your project’s selected SDK.

s.b: From your project directory: fvm flutter pub get fvm flutter run fvm flutter test fvm flutter build apk Choose the project's SDK with fvm use first. If the selected SDK is missing, install the version named in the error.

s.h: Check the version or get Flutter help
s.b: fvm flutter --version fvm flutter --help Everything after fvm flutter is passed to Flutter, including --help. A failing Flutter command returns the same exit status through FVM. To type just flutter, follow Shell Setup.

docs.d: Run the Dart version included with your selected Flutter SDK.

s.b: fvm dart --version fvm dart analyze fvm dart format . fvm dart run tool/generate.dart Run these from your project directory after selecting Flutter with fvm use. This uses Flutter's bundled Dart even if a separate Dart SDK is on PATH.
fvm dart --help All arguments after fvm dart go to Dart. Its exit status is returned unchanged. For scripts that need to find both Flutter and Dart themselves, use fvm exec.

docs.d: Run a tool or script with your selected Flutter and Dart on PATH.

s.b: fvm exec dart analyze fvm exec flutter test The command and any tools it starts find your selected Flutter SDK's flutter and dart first on PATH. Your terminal's PATH is unchanged after it finishes.

For a shell script that calls Flutter or Dart: fvm exec sh tool/check.sh Replace the script path with your own. All arguments after fvm exec belong to the command being run, including --help. FVM returns that command's exit status. Choose an SDK with fvm use before running the command.

docs.d: Make fvm and your project’s flutter command available in the terminal.

s.b: On macOS or Linux: fvm setup --write-path-line Setup creates the Flutter launcher and adds the required PATH entries to your shell startup file, backing it up first. Open a new terminal afterward. If fvm is not on PATH yet, use its full installed path. For the default macOS or Linux installation: "$HOME/.fvm/bin/fvm" setup --write-path-line

s.h: View instructions without editing your shell
s.b: fvm setup This creates the launcher and prints the PATH instructions. On Windows, add the printed directories to your user PATH manually; PowerShell does not support --write-path-line.

fvm setup --remove-path-line This removes the line added by setup, leaving your SDKs and manually added lines alone. Restart the terminal afterward. If you move the FVM executable, run setup from its new location. --fvm-path= lets you explicitly select the executable the launcher should use. See Shell Setup to verify the result.

docs.d: Find and fix problems with your FVM setup.

s.b: fvm doctor Run this from the affected project directory. Doctor checks your selected SDK, project configuration, editor link, and shell PATH. Follow the correction printed for each issue, then rerun the command.
fvm flutter doctor Use Flutter's doctor to check platform build tools and devices after FVM selects the right SDK. For missing commands or incorrect versions, see Troubleshooting.

docs.d: Choose when FVM uses colored terminal output.

s.b: fvm config color
fvm config color auto Choose auto, always, or never. auto adapts to the terminal and respects NO_COLOR and TERM=dumb.
fvm --color=never list This overrides the saved preference for that invocation. It controls FVM's output; Flutter and Dart control their own output.

docs.d: Install a newer FVM release while keeping your SDKs and project pins.

s.b: fvm update --check Reports whether a newer FVM release is available without installing it.
fvm update To choose a specific FVM release, run fvm update using a version from FVM releases. If updating fails, rerun the installer.
fvm update updates the manager. To move a project to a newer Flutter SDK, follow Updating FVM and Flutter.

docs.d: Choose the right Dart command when you also use standalone Dart.

s.h: Use Flutter's Dart for Flutter projects
s.b: fvm flutter --version fvm dart --version fvm dart analyze fvm dart uses the Dart included with your selected Flutter SDK. Plain dart continues to use your existing Dart setup, including DVM if you have installed it. For a script that calls both tools, run it with fvm exec so it finds the selected Flutter SDK's Flutter and Dart commands.

Use .fvmrc to select Flutter and set the editor's Flutter SDK path to .fvm/flutter_sdk. A .dvmrc selects standalone Dart; it does not select Flutter. FVM's shell setup adds a flutter launcher. It can coexist with DVM's dart launcher. See Shell Setup.

s.h: If you already have another FVM installed
s.b: These instructions are for mrgnhnt96/fvm, which is separate from the pub.dev package named fvm. Use the installation instructions here. Choose which fvm executable your PATH should use. If you keep both managers, give this one a separate FVM_HOME. Existing SDK caches are not imported; install the versions you need with fvm install. If commands reach the wrong manager, follow Troubleshooting.

docs.d: Install your project’s Flutter version and run tests in CI.

s.h: Install FVM and the project SDK
s.b: Commit .fvmrc with a concrete Flutter version. On a macOS or Linux runner, this example installs FVM, makes it available to the current shell, and tests a project pinned to 3.44.0: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrgnhnt96/fvm/main/install.sh sh export PATH="${FVM_HOME:-$HOME/.fvm}/bin:$PATH" fvm install 3.44.0 fvm flutter pub get fvm flutter test Replace 3.44.0 with the version in your project's .fvmrc. Run the Flutter commands from the checked-out project directory. For Windows runners, use the Windows installation steps. Use your CI provider's environment or PATH mechanism if installation and testing run in separate steps. A shell's export may not carry over to the next step. You do not need shell setup when invoking Flutter through fvm flutter. Use fvm exec for scripts that call Flutter or Dart themselves.

Cache $FVM_HOME/versions (default: ~/.fvm/versions) between jobs. Include the operating system, CPU architecture, and pinned Flutter version in the cache key. Keep the install command so a job also works with an empty cache.
Install the version before overriding the project pin. In a POSIX shell: fvm install 3.44.0 FVM_FLUTTER_VERSION=3.44.0 fvm flutter test A failing Flutter command returns a failing exit status to CI.

docs.d: Update FVM and choose when your projects move to newer Flutter releases.

s.b: fvm update --check fvm update --check reports whether an update is available. fvm update installs it. Your Flutter SDKs and project pins stay in place. You can also rerun the installer. To install a specific FVM release, use fvm update with a version from FVM releases.

From your project directory: fvm install stable fvm use stable fvm flutter --version fvm flutter pub get fvm flutter test The first command downloads the current stable release. The second updates .fvmrc and your editor's SDK link. Commit the changed .fvmrc after checking your app. For a specific release, use fvm use instead. Other projects keep their saved versions.

s.h: Update the default for unpinned directories
s.b: fvm install stable fvm global stable
Use --no-version-check for a command where you do not want FVM update notices: fvm --no-version-check flutter test

docs.d: Fix missing commands, incorrect Flutter versions, and editor setup.

s.h: The fvm command is not found
s.b: With the default macOS or Linux installation, run: "$HOME/.fvm/bin/fvm" setup --write-path-line Open a new terminal and run fvm --version. For a custom installation, use the executable path printed by the installer. On Windows, add the directories printed by setup to your user PATH, then open a new terminal. If the executable is missing, install FVM again.

An old shell function, alias, or PATH entry may take priority. Run the installed executable by its full path with doctor, for example: "$HOME/.fvm/bin/fvm" doctor Remove the conflicting setup identified in the output, rerun setup, and open a new terminal.

fvm which fvm doctor Check whether FVM_FLUTTER_VERSION, a parent .fvmrc, or your global default is selecting the version. Change the project version with fvm use . If fvm flutter --version is correct but flutter --version is not, repeat Shell Setup. The FVM launcher must come first on PATH.

Run the fvm install command printed in the error. For a new project checkout, run fvm use with the version from .fvmrc to install it and create the editor link. If FVM does not recognize stable or beta, install that channel first: fvm install stable fvm use stable

Check your network connection and proxy settings, then retry. FVM downloads its own updates from GitHub and Flutter SDKs from Google's Flutter storage. For a damaged SDK, reinstall its version: fvm install 3.44.0 --force If the release is unavailable for your computer, use fvm list-remote to find a supported version. If a checksum mismatch persists, do not use that download.

Run fvm use again and set the editor's Flutter SDK path to .fvm/flutter_sdk beside .fvmrc. Restart the editor. See Quick Start for the VS Code setting. If Windows reports that it cannot create the SDK link, follow the error's instructions about permissions or Developer Mode, then rerun fvm use.
Use fvm dart --version to check the Dart bundled with your project's Flutter SDK. Plain dart may use a separate installation.
fvm --verbose flutter --version Use this alongside fvm doctor when you need more detail about a failure.
